message:
fix(update): a host that is leaving is not a host that refused

Three of four attempts on 2026-09-11 ended AbandonedBeforeSwap with "could not ask
pid 7332 to stop", about a process that had acknowledged the handoff seventy
milliseconds earlier and was standing down. Enumeration and request are two moments
and the window went away in between. A failed request is now checked against the
process: if it is genuinely gone, that is the outcome this step wanted. A live target
that refuses is still a failure and nothing is terminated -- both halves are tested,
because without the second the first would excuse every refusal.

The fourth attempt failed differently and worse. Health stayed pending for thirty
seconds and the update rolled back, while the host had been online the entire time --
the child printed "directory online" one second after it started. write_health_report
turned ok only when the log uploader had sent a batch, which is a different subsystem
with its own credentials and schedule. The report said it was waiting for the
directory and was waiting for something else.

The child's stdout already passes through the host -- a comment in the same file says
it is the only place the directory result is reported -- so that line now sets health.
The uploader still counts, whichever arrives first. The thirty second budget is
unchanged; raising it would have hidden this.
